The '''Bespin Wing Guard''', informally known as the '''Bespin Security Guard''', '''Cloud City Wing Guard''', or '''Cloud Police''', whose members sometimes were called '''Bespin [[Police officer/Legends|cops]]''',<ref name="Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref> was the primary [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|security force]] of [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]].<ref name="DB">{{DB|organization|bespinwingguard|Wing Guard}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Lobot-TCG_EoD.jpg|thumb|left|225px|[[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]] leads the Bespin Wing Guard]]
The Wing Guard comprised the largest segment of [[Cloud City Control]],<ref name="ESBJN">[[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' junior novelization]]</ref> and was placed under the command of the [[Baron Administrator/Legends|Baron Administrator]] of Cloud City, the city's [[Cloud City Central Computer|central computer]], or the Administrator's cyborg aide [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]]. The [[Police officer/Legends|Security Guards]] operated out of the [[Cloud City Security Tower]].<ref name="DB" />

Wing Guards were not simply security guards on Cloud City; officers had a range of duties, from police to meteorologists, customs inspectors, and crisis controllers. Despite this array of multi-tasking, the Wing Guard was at one time highly disorganized and corrupt. It took the efforts of [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] to reshape his security forces into a streamlined organization. One of the new Administrator's changes was to alter the Wing Guard wages based on public perception of their effectiveness; he also hired a squadron of "commando pilots" to help protect the city.<ref name="DB" />

[[File:Lando_turns_the_tables.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Bespin guards turn on the Empire]]
Though the Wing Guard continued to serve Cloud City after Calrissian's departure with members of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], small pockets of corruption grew among the security forces during the rule of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. This was thought to have been caused by the overflow of criminal activity on Cloud City, particularly during the time of [[Desann]]'s assault on the [[New Jedi Order]]. During this time, Cloud City was held under siege by the [[Empire Reborn]]. The Wing Guards fought back, and several fought alongside [[Kyle Katarn]] when the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] helped [[Battle of Bespin (Empire Reborn)|liberate]] the city.<ref name="SW:JKII:JO">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]''</ref>

==Uniforms==
[[File:Lando13.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Wing Guards present when the ''Millennium Falcon'' arrived at Cloud City in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].]]
Wing Guards dressed in royal blue uniforms with red and gold trim and had royal blue helmets. They also carried silver [[Relby-k23 blaster pistol]]s.<ref name="DB" /> During a [[Rescue of Garm Bel Iblis|conflict]] against the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Chop'aa Notimo]] and his [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] henchmen, the Wing Guards under Lobot wielded [[A280 blaster rifle/Legends|A280 blaster rifles]].<ref name="The Force Unleashed">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Cloud City security blaster pistols were manufactured from pneumatic spear guns. They were detailed with model kit parts from a V-8 engine and an [[Wikipedia:F-4 Phantom II|F-4E Phantom II jet]], along with a plastic coffee stirrer.<ref name="Star Wars Magazine UK 66">[[Star Wars: The Official Magazine 66|''Star Wars: The Official Magazine'' 66]]</ref>

John Mollo's original costume sketch for the Bespin Wing Guards was considerably more elaborate than what ended up in the film.
